title: User Journey Map (Creator)
purpose: Mermaid Journey diagram showing a creator's experience through 7 key milestones from signup through contest management, with emotional scoring and friction annotations.
audience: Product managers, UX designers, creator growth team, QA engineers
description: The creator user journey spans 7 milestones: Signup + verification (score 2), First content upload (score 3), Subscriber notification (score 3), Earnings dashboard (score 4), Payout request (score 2), Message fans (score 4), Run contest (score 4). Critical friction: Payout off-ramp is fully mocked with no real money received. Medium friction: Verification is manual with no status updates, synchronous thumbnail generation slows upload (1GB memory buffer per file), no real-time push for subscriber notifications, broadcast has N+1 query pattern, contest winner uses Math.random() with no verifiable fairness. The journey reveals that the creator's core financial incentive (payout) has the worst experience, undermining the platform's value proposition.

preconditions: Creator has valid email and password for signup
Platform is accessible with working frontend and backend
Creator has valid government ID for verification
postconditions: Creator is onboarded with subscription tiers, verified identity, and active status
Creator has published content with notifications sent to subscribers
Creator has viewed earnings, requested payout (mocked), messaged fans, and run a contest

nodes.label: Signup + verification — Select role → upload docs → wait
nodes.description: Creator signs up, selects creator role, completes onboarding (bio, tiers, banner), and submits identity verification. Score: 2. Manual admin review.

nodes.label: Select creator role during signup
nodes.description: User selects 'creator' role in signup form — determines redirect to onboarding flow

nodes.label: Complete onboarding (bio, tiers, banner)
nodes.description: POST /api/v1/users/me/onboarding — bio, subscription tiers, banner image. Backend syncs tiers with Stripe.

nodes.label: Upload verification docs (ID, selfie, signature)
nodes.description: POST /api/v1/users/me/verification — government ID photo, selfie, electronic signature uploaded to R2 private bucket

nodes.label: Admin reviews and approves/rejects
nodes.description: Admin reviews verification documents via signed URLs, approves (status=active) or rejects (status=previous)

nodes.label: No status update notifications during review
nodes.description: Creator sees only 'awaiting review' — no real-time updates when admin acts

nodes.label: First content upload — Drag file → caption → publish
nodes.description: Creator uploads media files with title, type, visibility, optional AI caption. Score: 3. Sync thumbnail gen slows upload.

nodes.label: Select media files (up to 10)
nodes.description: Creator drags or selects image/video/audio files via file picker

nodes.label: Add title, type, visibility, AI caption
nodes.description: Creator enters title, selects content type, sets visibility (subscribers_only/PPV), optionally generates AI caption

nodes.label: POST /api/v1/content multipart upload
nodes.description: Frontend sends multipart form with files + metadata to backend (uploadContent middleware, 1GB limit, 10 file limit)

nodes.label: Backend file processing (sharp/ffmpeg)
nodes.description: Images: sharp resize + watermark + WebP conversion. Video: ffmpeg thumbnail (1s, 400px). All files uploaded to R2.

nodes.label: Sync thumbnail generation slows upload (1GB buffer)
nodes.description: Sharp/ffmpeg processing is synchronous in-process — large files block the event loop, 1GB memory buffer per file

nodes.label: Content record created in database
nodes.description: Content model creates record with file metadata array, visibility, status

nodes.label: Upload failure (file too large, unsupported format)
nodes.description: Multer rejects >1GB files (413), sharp/ffmpeg rejects unsupported formats (500)

nodes.label: Subscriber notification — Content published → notified
nodes.description: If subscribers_only: subscribers notified via DB notification. Score: 3. No real-time push (fan sees on next page load).

nodes.label: Check if content is subscribers_only
nodes.description: Content service checks visibility field after content creation

nodes.label: Fetch all active subscribers
nodes.description: Notification service fetches all subscriptions with status=active for this creator

nodes.label: Filter by notification preferences
nodes.description: Check each subscriber's preferences.notifications.newContent flag

nodes.label: Batch create notification records in DB
nodes.description: Create notification records for eligible subscribers — no Socket.IO broadcast, user sees on next page load

nodes.label: No real-time push to subscribers
nodes.description: Notifications are DB-only — no socket event or push notification sent

nodes.label: Earnings dashboard — View earnings → see balance
nodes.description: Creator visits /hub/earnings to view total earned, pending, available balance. Score: 4. Earnings data is accurate.

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/creator/dashboard
nodes.description: Frontend requests dashboard — backend aggregates subscriber count, new content, views, recent earnings, PPV revenue

nodes.label: View earnings breakdown
nodes.description: GET /api/v1/creator/earnings — backend returns earnings data with subscription/tip/PPV breakdowns

nodes.label: Payout request — Enter amount → submit → off-ramp
nodes.description: Creator requests payout for available balance. Score: 2. Off-ramp is fully mocked — no real money received.

nodes.label: Enter payout amount
nodes.description: Creator enters amount to withdraw from available balance

nodes.label: POST /api/v1/creator/payouts
nodes.description: Frontend sends payout request — creator service checks balance, creates negative transaction

nodes.label: Off-ramp returns fake transfer ID
nodes.description: processDebitCardOffRamp — creates transaction record but returns mock response: { transferId: 'mock_cb_...', estimatedArrival: 'In 5-10 minutes' }

nodes.label: No real money received — fully simulated
nodes.description: No actual Stripe/Coinbase integration called — creator sees confirmation but never receives funds

nodes.label: No balance locking — race condition possible
nodes.description: Multiple concurrent payout requests could exceed available balance (no DB lock)

nodes.label: Message fans — View conversations → DM → broadcast
nodes.description: Creator manages DMs and sends broadcast to all subscribers. Score: 4. Broadcast has N+1 query pattern.

nodes.label: View fan conversations
nodes.description: GET /api/v1/messages/conversations — list conversations with last message preview and unread count

nodes.label: Send direct message to fan
nodes.description: POST /api/v1/messages — message delivered via Socket.IO in real-time

nodes.label: Send broadcast to all subscribers
nodes.description: POST /api/v1/messages/mass-message — backend iterates all active subscribers (N+1 problem)

nodes.label: N+1 query pattern in broadcast
nodes.description: For each subscriber: find or create conversation, insert message, emit socket event — no batch operation

nodes.label: Run contest — Create → set prize → select winner → announce
nodes.description: Creator creates, publishes, and finalizes a contest. Score: 4. Math.random() winner selection with no audit trail.

nodes.label: Create contest as draft
nodes.description: POST /api/v1/contests — creator sets title, description, start/end dates, prize, entry requirements

nodes.label: Publish contest (draft -> active)
nodes.description: PUT /api/v1/contests/:id/publish — contest becomes visible in feed, fans can enter

nodes.label: Finalize and select winner
nodes.description: POST /api/v1/contests/:id/finalize — backend selects winner using Math.random()

nodes.label: Math.random() winner selection — no audit trail
nodes.description: Winner selection uses Math.random() with no verifiable randomness, no on-chain commit-reveal, no audit trail

nodes.label: Winner announced
nodes.description: Winner recorded on contest record, notification sent to winner

validationRules: Creator must complete onboarding before publishing content
Verification requires both ID photo and selfie photo
Content file count max 10, individual file size max 1GB
Supported MIME types: jpeg, png, webp, mp4, mov, mp3, m4a, wav, ogg
Contest start_date must be before end_date
Payout amount cannot exceed available balance
businessRules: Platform commission is 12.5% DEFAULT_COMMISSION_RATE on all transactions
Enclave creators get 10% commission (not yet implemented)
Verification status must be 'active' for full platform access
Subscription tiers are synced with Stripe during onboarding
securityConsiderations: Payout has no balance lock — concurrent requests could exceed available balance
AI caption sends base64 image to OpenAI/OpenRouter without explicit user consent
Verification documents stored in R2 accessed via 60-second signed URLs — temporary exposure window
Math.random() for contest winner is not cryptographically secure — no audit trail
performanceConsiderations: Sync thumbnail generation (sharp/ffmpeg) blocks the event loop — 1GB memory buffer per file
Broadcast message has N+1 query pattern — one query per subscriber
Dashboard aggregates 5 data sources per page load — no caching
AI caption API call takes 1-5 seconds synchronous HTTP wait
annotations: Payout: score 2 — off-ramp is fully mocked, no real money received
Signup: score 2 — verification process is manual with no status updates
Upload: score 3 — synchronous thumbnail generation slows upload, 1GB memory buffer per file
Notify: score 3 — no real-time push to subscribers (DB-only)
Messaging: score 4 — broadcast has N+1 query pattern
Contest: score 4 — Math.random() winner selection with no verifiable fairness

legend.meaning: Average experience (Upload, Notify — functional but slow)
